description: Memorandum and Articles of Association not filed with RJSC. Section 11: constitutional documents required. Without filing, company has no valid constitution.
Paid-up capital exceeds authorized capital. Section 150: company cannot issue shares beyond authorized capital. All excess allotments void.
Annual audit not completed before AGM. Section 151: directors must lay audited accounts at AGM. Presenting unaudited accounts renders adoption invalid and exposes directors to liability.

basis: Section 85(2)(b), Companies Act 1994 (Bangladesh), subject to current Articles
description: Private-company quorum default is two members where total membership is up to six and three where it exceeds six, unless the current Articles provide otherwise. Current Articles, member register and attendance evidence must be verified; counsel approval remains pending.
AGM held but minutes not prepared or signed by chairman. Section 83: minutes are prima facie evidence of proceedings. Without minutes, AGM validity can be challenged.

Director appointment not filed via Form XII within 14 days. Section 92 requires 14-day filing (NOT 30 days). Until filed, third parties cannot verify director authority, invalidating contracts and resolutions.

Director resignation/removal/death not filed via Form XII within 14 days. Section 92 requires 14-day filing. Until filed, departed director remains on public record as active, creating liability for post-departure obligations.

Director change unfiled for over 1 year. Continuing offence under Section 92. Prolonged non-filing creates compounding personal liability. Each day of default adds to statutory fine. Board resolutions may be challenged.
Share allotment not filed via Form XV within 30 days. Section 50 requires return of allotment. Failure means allotment not reflected in RJSC register, creating uncertainty about issued capital.

Share certificates not issued within 60 days of allotment. Section 46 requires certificates within 2 months. Non-issuance means no documentary evidence of ownership, obstructing transfers and dividends.
Capital increase not filed via Form IV within 30 days of special resolution. Section 52 requires notice of increase. Unrecorded increases cause RJSC records to differ from actual capital.
Share transfer without Form 117 instrument. Section 108 requires proper instrument of transfer, duly stamped, executed by both parties. Missing instrument renders transfer void and unregistrable.

Share transfer without board approval where AoA restricts transfer. Section 47 + AoA: board approval required. Transfer in breach is void; transferee has no legal title. Register cannot be validly updated.

One or more of 7 mandatory statutory registers not maintained at registered office. Required: Members (Sec 34), Directors (Sec 90), Charges (Sec 87), Transfers (Sec 108), Debentures (Sec 90), AGM Minutes (Sec 83), Board Minutes (Sec 90). Failure is criminal offence; officers personally liable.

Capital alteration without required board/special resolution, or forms not filed. Section 54 governs capital increase procedure. Unrecorded changes cause RJSC register to differ from actual capital, creating legal uncertainty.
Capital reduction without court order. Section 100: court confirmation required. Without it, reduction is void, directors personally liable.

Special resolution passed but not filed within 30 days. Section 87: every special resolution must be filed. Unfiled resolution not binding on company or enforceable against third parties. Includes capital increase, MoA/AoA alteration, voluntary winding up.

Compliance profile shows RJSC strike-off criteria under Section 304: multi-year missed filings, no recent trading, or RED flags across 3+ modules. Section 304 permits strike-off for non-filing or non-trading. Structured Regularization required immediately.

Immediate RJSC strike-off risk. Criteria: 3+ years non-filing, strike-off notice received, or on published strike-off list. Once struck off: company ceases to exist, contracts void, accounts frozen. AGM adjourned without proper notice. Section 84.
Charge satisfaction not filed via Form XIX. Section 87.
Unresolved penalty notices. Section 447: fine up to Tk 10,000 per offence.
